400.title: Polimex Mostostal to Build Two AP1000 Assembly Halls in Poland
400.summary: Polimex Mostostal has signed a contract to build two assembly halls for the construction site of the Lubiatowo-Kopalino nuclear power plant in northern Poland.
400.body: Polimex Mostostal has signed a contract to build two assembly halls for the construction site of the Lubiatowo-Kopalino nuclear power plant in northern Poland. The agreement covers the supply of a key element of the production and assembly facilities needed to build the three Westinghouse AP1000 units commissioned by Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ), the state-owned company overseeing the project. A Project Described as Unprecedented in Poland According to Leszek Hołda, chief executive officer of Bechtel Polska, building the two assembly halls, each as tall as a 12-storey office building and with a footprint larger than a football pitch, is a project that is almost unprecedented in Poland. Poland's Nuclear Project Has Been Taking Shape Since 2022 In November 2022, the Polish government of the time selected Westinghouse's AP1000 reactor technology for the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site in the Choczewo municipality in Pomerania, in northern Poland.

400.title: Greenvolt and Statkraft sign agreement for management of 400 MW of BESS in Poland
400.summary: Statkraft, Europe’s largest producer of renewable energy and a leading PPA provider in Europe, and Greenvolt Power, a global utility scale developer of onshore wind, solar, and battery storage projects, have signed a 10-year tolling agreement covering 400 MW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across two projects in Poland.
400.body: Statkraft, Europe’s largest producer of renewable energy and a leading PPA provider in Europe, and Greenvolt Power, a global utility scale developer of onshore wind, solar, and battery storage projects, have signed a 10-year tolling agreement covering 400 MW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across two projects in Poland. The agreement is the largest publicly communicated in the EU to date and marks Statkraft’s first large scale BESS contract in the Polish market. The structure of a tolling agreement gives Statkraft the right to decide when the batteries charge and discharge across energy and flexibility markets, while giving Greenvolt an additional source of predictable, long-term revenue alongside the revenue already secured through Poland’s Capacity Market. Kornel Koronowski, Head of Origination Poland, Statkraft, commented: “Our partnership with Greenvolt shows our ambition in Poland.
